summary.intent: Land a set of in-flight caliper PRs (#345, #346, #347, #348) by scaling back overreaching fixes and resolving merge conflicts, avoid repeating the conflict pattern, then analyze narration, stale docs and truly dead code and prepare a trail and PR for the cleanup.
summary.outcome: #345, #348, #343, #353 and #346 merged; #347 was conflict-resolved and is mergeable with gates passing. A three-pass read-only cleanup analysis was done and spot-checked, scheduling rules were saved to memory, trails #234 (docs and dead code cleanup) and #235 (known gaps and decisions) were created, and a worker was started on the docs correction branch.

repo: Entire Gates has four sub-gates (approvals, checks, findings, up-to-date). A failing Entire Gates on #346/#347 was only the missing approval, not open findings; open findings below the blocking threshold do not fail it.
Entire `trail merge` defers branch deletion to GitHub's auto-delete setting for GitHub-backed trails, and GitHub closes a child PR if its parent branch is deleted without retargeting.
`extractor/tests.rs` and `pipeline/tests.rs` are repeat conflict hotspots because every PR appends tests at the same spot; `provider.ts` and `weekly.py` behave the same way.

Name resolution has two owners: the resolver has a real scope model, while the extractor keys enums, aliases and classes by bare name with ad hoc counters like `local_depth`. This caused repeated review rounds on scoping.
Snapshot tests fail in worktrees without `node_modules` or when nested under the caliper checkout (path-prefix differences); clean-room worktrees with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` pass.
CLAUDE.md contains only the Entire block and never imports AGENTS.md, so Claude Code never loaded the repo rule 'comments: only the non-obvious why, no history'.
`CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` was bumped 29 to 30 when cached `SourceData` gained `enum_declarations`; the golden fixture and snapshot must be updated with it.

Dead-code scan of main found only 5 confirmed-dead items. Narration is small (53 items plus 100 SPEC/AC tag lines), while docs are the real cleanup (54 records, 91 stale `file.rs:NNN` refs in docs/architecture).

Several public-API items look like unfinished features rather than dead code: `DefaultSource::JsDoc`, `DiagnosticCode::ComputedDefault`, `MalformedFrameReason::InvalidJson`, and `ImportRef.is_type_only` (whose logic overlaps #347's `imports_a_value`).

code.finding: `visit_static_block` bumps `local_depth` like `visit_block_statement`; after merging main both sides had defined these methods (E0201), resolved by one method each incrementing `block_depth` and `local_depth`.
`names_an_enum` now checks the `enum_declarations` set instead of `global.enums`, so `as const` objects of the same name don't count as enums.
Doc comment says checker methods are not wired up yet, but `crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs` already calls them.
The `TSOptionalType` (`T?`) branch still wraps in `Union([T, Undefined])`, which is dead since `resolve_union` strips undefined at render.

workflow: Run overlapping PRs one at a time in merge order and start each worker from current main; parallelize only on disjoint files. Resolving two PRs against main in parallel guaranteed a second conflict.
Read the gate breakdown (approvals, checks, findings, up-to-date) rather than counting findings or trusting the aggregate check status.
After two review rounds on the same code, choose a root-cause fix, a scale-back, or a documented limitation instead of patching the next repro.
Spot-check subagent claims against the checkout before relying on them; subagent reports are not user authority.
Merges can compile-break without textual conflicts (duplicate methods, changed signatures), so a clean-room build and test run after conflict resolution is needed.
Stacked PRs: link with `entire trail link --base`, merge bottom-up with merge commits, never squash, never merge a child into its parent branch.

friction: Merge conflicts kept recurring on #346/#347 because many workers produced overlapping PRs and merges made the others stale; the user pushed back sharply.
The assistant misread the failing Entire Gates as a serious review finding, and chased findings on PRs whose gate only lacked approval.
The permission classifier denied the #345 worker's `entire trail finding dismiss` as an external write, though it allowed it for other workers.
Subagents hit worktree issues: a branch already checked out elsewhere, a mistaken `git reset --hard` that was restored, and snapshot tests failing in worktrees without `node_modules`.
The #345 scale-back still left 6 open findings, including real accuracy concerns about conditional/optional tuple elements, so it needed a second scale-back proposal.
The assistant's 'main moved' wording was unclear to the user, who is the sole merger.
`gh` was blocked in the analysis sandbox, and a dead-code run showed 20 unexplained intermittent core `--lib` failures.
open_items: Docs correction branch `docs/correct-stale-docs` is in progress; assistant must verify it, then open the PR via the gh shim (needs the user's Touch ID).
Later cleanup PRs: 53 non-test comment rewrites, test comments plus 100 SPEC/AC tag lines, the `rdt-coverage.md` trim, and dated-log trims.
User decisions pending: keep or remove SPEC tags and archive the done specs; remove or wire the four unused public items; delete or label `benchmarks.md` historical; add `@AGENTS.md` to CLAUDE.md.
Model decisions: whether `DefaultValue` records provenance (JsDoc/ComputedDefault diagnostics), whether bad JSON frames should surface as recoverable errors, and who owns type-only import logic.
Scoping/name-resolution architecture: a design note (ADR) and read-only investigation, with exclusive ownership of extractor/resolver files, after #346/#347 land.
Documented limitations: function-local interfaces, enums and classes keyed by bare name, optional tuple markers, conditionals over shadowed type parameters, interfaces in switch cases.
Loose ends tracked in trail #235: unpushed #367 follow-up (4e588a71), `perf/cycles-by-structure`, the 13 finding dismissals, the 0.9.0 release call, Callisto #442.
#345's wip work is preserved on `wip/css-tuple-full`; the user must run two stale-finding dismissals on caliper/142; reconsider limiting tuple resolution to plain/labelled members.
Possible follow-ups: split append-hotspot test files into per-feature modules, consider a merge queue, and tighten 68 over-wide `pub` items (recommended against).
